Week 12 Lab Programs

1. Prompt Engineering

AIM

To understand and implement prompt engineering techniques in Artificial Intelligence by designing effective and structured prompts. The objective is to improve the quality, accuracy, and relevance of AI-generated responses by providing clear instructions, appropriate context, and specific requirements to obtain meaningful outputs from AI language models.

DESCRIPTION

Prompt Engineering is the process of creating and refining instructions given to AI models to generate desired outputs. It involves techniques such as zero-shot prompting, few-shot prompting, role-based prompting, and chain-of-thought prompting. Effective prompts help AI systems understand user requirements and produce accurate, relevant, and meaningful responses.

CODE

A. Image question answering using BLIP

import requests
from PIL import Image
from transformers import BlipProcessor, BlipForQuestionAnswering

processor = BlipProcessor.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-vqa-base")
model = BlipForQuestionAnswering.from_pretrained("Salesforce/blip-vqa-base")

img_url = "try any image"
raw_image = Image.open((img_url)).convert('RGB')

question = "what is the colour of women?"
inputs = processor(raw_image, question, return_tensors="pt")

out = model.generate(**inputs)
print(processor.decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True))

B. Object detection using DETR

from transformers import DetrImageProcessor, DetrForObjectDetection
import torch
from PIL import Image
import requests

url = "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"
image = Image.open(requests.get(url, stream=True).raw)

# You can specify the revision tag if you don't want the timm dependency
processor = DetrImageProcessor.from_pretrained("facebook/detr-resnet-50", revision="no_timm")
model = DetrForObjectDetection.from_pretrained("facebook/detr-resnet-50", revision="no_timm")

inputs = processor(images=image, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)

# Convert outputs (bounding boxes and class logits) to COCO API format
# Let's only keep detections with score > 0.9
target_sizes = torch.tensor([image.size[::-1]])
results = processor.post_process_object_detection(
    outputs, target_sizes=target_sizes, threshold=0.9
)[0]

for score, label, box in zip(results["scores"], results["labels"], results["boxes"]):
    box = [round(i, 2) for i in box.tolist()]
    print(
        f"Detected {model.config.id2label[label.item()]} with confidence "
        f"{round(score.item(), 3)} at location {box}"
    )

C. Image detection with bounding boxes

!pip install opencv-python-headless matplotlib transformers torch requests

from transformers import DetrImageProcessor, DetrForObjectDetection
import torch
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import requests
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the image from the URL
url = "http://images.cocodataset.org/val2017/000000039769.jpg"
image_pil = Image.open(requests.get(url, stream=True).raw)
image_np = np.array(image_pil)

# Initialize the processor and model
processor = DetrImageProcessor.from_pretrained(
    "facebook/detr-resnet-50", revision="no_timm"
)
model = DetrForObjectDetection.from_pretrained(
    "facebook/detr-resnet-50", revision="no_timm"
)

# Process the image
inputs = processor(images=image_pil, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)

# Convert outputs to COCO API format and filter detections with score > 0.9
target_sizes = torch.tensor([image_pil.size[::-1]])
results = processor.post_process_object_detection(
    outputs, target_sizes=target_sizes, threshold=0.9
)[0]

# Draw rectangles on the image using OpenCV
for score, label, box in zip(results["scores"], results["labels"], results["boxes"]):
    box = [int(i) for i in box.tolist()]
    label_text = model.config.id2label[label.item()]
    color = (0, 255, 0)  # Green color for the rectangle
    thickness = 2
    cv2.rectangle(image_np, (box[0], box[1]), (box[2], box[3]), color, thickness)

D. Image detection with labels

!pip install opencv-python-headless matplotlib transformers torch requests

from transformers import DetrImageProcessor, DetrForObjectDetection
import torch
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import requests
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the image
url = "/content/images.jpg"
image_pil = Image.open(url)
image_np = np.array(image_pil)

# Initialize the processor and model
processor = DetrImageProcessor.from_pretrained(
    "facebook/detr-resnet-50", revision="no_timm"
)
model = DetrForObjectDetection.from_pretrained(
    "facebook/detr-resnet-50", revision="no_timm"
)

# Process the image
inputs = processor(images=image_pil, return_tensors="pt")
outputs = model(**inputs)

# Convert outputs to COCO API format and filter detections with score > 0.9
target_sizes = torch.tensor([image_pil.size[::-1]])
results = processor.post_process_object_detection(
    outputs, target_sizes=target_sizes, threshold=0.9
)[0]

# Draw rectangles and labels
for score, label, box in zip(results["scores"], results["labels"], results["boxes"]):
    box = [int(i) for i in box.tolist()]
    label_text = model.config.id2label[label.item()]
    color = (0, 255, 0)  # Green color for the rectangle
    thickness = 2
    cv2.rectangle(image_np, (box[0], box[1]), (box[2], box[3]), color, thickness)

    text = f"{label_text}: {round(score.item(), 3)}"
    cv2.putText(image_np, text, (box[0], box[1] - 10),
                cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.5, color, 2)

# Convert BGR to RGB for displaying with matplotlib
image_rgb = cv2.cvtColor(image_np, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)

# Display the image using matplotlib
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))
plt.imshow(image_rgb)
plt.axis('off')
plt.show()

)

2. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)

AIM

To study and implement Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in Artificial Intelligence for image processing and recognition tasks. The objective is to understand how CNNs automatically extract important features from images using convolution and pooling layers, enabling accurate classification, object detection, and visual pattern recognition in various real-world applications.

DESCRIPTION

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are deep learning models primarily used for processing visual data. They consist of convolutional, pooling, and fully connected layers. Convolution layers extract features, pooling layers reduce dimensionality, and fully connected layers perform classification. CNNs are widely used in facial recognition, medical imaging, and object detection applications.

CODE

A. Download and locate the cats-versus-dogs dataset

%pip install -q --upgrade kagglehub

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from google.colab import userdata

download_dir = Path("/content/dogs-vs-cats")
download_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
download_complete = download_dir / ".download_complete"

if not download_complete.is_file():
    token = userdata.get("KAGGLE_API_KEY").strip()
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("The Colab secret KAGGLE_API_KEY is empty.")

    subprocess.run(
        [
            "kaggle", "datasets", "download",
            "-d", "salader/dogs-vs-cats",
            "--path", str(download_dir),
            "--unzip", "--force",
        ],
        env={**os.environ, "KAGGLE_API_TOKEN": token},
        check=True,
    )

train_folders = sorted(
    download_dir.rglob("train"),
    key=lambda path: (len(path.parts), str(path)),
)

dataset_dir = next(
    (
        folder.parent
        for folder in train_folders
        if all(
            (folder.parent / split / class_name).is_dir()
            for split in ("train", "test")
            for class_name in ("cats", "dogs")
        )
    ),
    None,
)

if dataset_dir is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"Could not find train/cats, train/dogs, test/cats and test/dogs "
        f"under {download_dir}."
    )

download_complete.touch()
print(f"Dataset directory: {dataset_dir}")

B. Load dataset, build and train the CNN model

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers

IMAGE_SIZE = (256, 256)
BATCH_SIZE = 32
CLASS_NAMES = ["cats", "dogs"]

dataset_options = {
    "labels": "inferred",
    "label_mode": "binary",
    "class_names": CLASS_NAMES,
    "color_mode": "rgb",
    "image_size": IMAGE_SIZE,
    "batch_size": BATCH_SIZE,
}

train_ds = keras.utils.image_dataset_from_directory(
    dataset_dir / "train",
    shuffle=True,
    seed=42,
    **dataset_options,
)

validation_ds = keras.utils.image_dataset_from_directory(
    dataset_dir / "test",
    shuffle=False,
    **dataset_options,
)

print("Class labels:", dict(enumerate(CLASS_NAMES)))

model = keras.Sequential([
    layers.Input(shape=(*IMAGE_SIZE, 3)),
    layers.Rescaling(1.0 / 255),

    layers.Conv2D(32, 3, activation="relu"),
    layers.BatchNormalization(),
    layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=2),

    layers.Conv2D(64, 3, activation="relu"),
    layers.BatchNormalization(),
    layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=2),

    layers.Conv2D(128, 3, activation="relu"),
    layers.BatchNormalization(),
    layers.MaxPooling2D(pool_size=2),

    layers.Flatten(),
    layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"),
    layers.Dropout(0.1),
    layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"),
    layers.Dropout(0.1),
    layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid"),
])

model.compile(
    optimizer="adam",
    loss="binary_crossentropy",
    metrics=["accuracy"],
)

model.summary()

history = model.fit(
    train_ds,
    validation_data=validation_ds,
    epochs=10,
)

C. Upload an image and predict whether it is a cat or dog (PDF page 8)

from google.colab import files

uploaded = files.upload()

if len(uploaded) != 1:
    raise ValueError("Upload exactly one image.")

image_name, image_bytes = next(iter(uploaded.items()))

image = tf.io.decode_image(
    image_bytes,
    channels=3,
    expand_animations=False,
)
resized_image = tf.image.resize(image, IMAGE_SIZE, method="bilinear")
batch = tf.expand_dims(resized_image, axis=0)

dog_score = float(model.predict(batch, verbose=0)[0, 0])
prediction = "Dog" if dog_score >= 0.5 else "Cat"

print(f"{image_name}: {prediction}")
print(f"Cat score: {1 - dog_score:.1%} | Dog score: {dog_score:.1%}")

plt.imshow(image.numpy())
plt.axis("off")
plt.show()
